args.reason: The webhookUrl validation calls .toLowerCase() on line 46, which transforms the user's Zapier URL from 'https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/1234567/AbCdEfG/' to 'https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/1234567/abcdefg/'. Zapier catch hooks are case-sensitive in their path component, so lowercasing the URL breaks the webhook endpoint, causing the 404 'hook not found' errors. The admin sees the original mixed-case URL in the settings form (stored correctly in the database), but every outgoing webhook attempt uses the lowercased version that was saved.

answer.overlooked_assumption: The agent assumed that lowercasing the webhook URL would preserve its validity, but Zapier webhook URLs contain case-sensitive path segments that become invalid when lowercased.
answer.why_it_breaks: The agent applied .toLowerCase() to the webhookUrl field (line 46) following the same pattern used for email addresses and slugs. However, the Zapier webhook URL https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/1234567/AbCdEfG/ contains a case-sensitive path segment 'AbCdEfG' that becomes 'abcdefg' after lowercasing, causing Zapier to return HTTP 404 because the hook identifier no longer matches.
